body.statement:
Equip \(\mathscr K\) with the product of Euclidean distance for \((p_x)_x\),
uniform distance on \(\mathcal A\) for every \(f_x,q_x\), and any metric for
weak convergence of \(Q_1,Q_2\).  Then \(\mathscr K\) is compact.  Along
convergent sequences in this metric, \(\phi_{Q_j}\) converges uniformly on
every compact frequency interval, the fitted probability and marked channels
converge locally uniformly on \(\mathbb R^2\), and
\(\vartheta\mapsto\mu_\vartheta\) is continuous from \(\mathscr K\) to
\(C(I)\).  For every \(n\), the exact feasible set
\(\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)\) is compact, and its finitely many
constraint-violation functions are measurable in \(z\) and continuous in
\(\vartheta\).
body.proof_tex:
By \(\textnormal{def:exact-projected-class}\), every signal coordinate has support in the same compact interval \(\mathcal A=[-B_A,B_A]\), and its \(H^\beta\)-norm is bounded by either \(R_f\) or \(R_q\).  We first prove compactness of these signal coordinates.  Use the Fourier convention
\[
 \|g\|_{H^\beta}^2
 =\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^2)^\beta
       |\widehat g(t)|^2\,dt.
\]
Fourier inversion and Cauchy--Schwarz imply, first for smooth functions and then, by approximation in \(H^\beta\), for every \(g\in H^\beta(\mathbb R)\),
\[
 |g(a)|
 \le \frac{\|g\|_{H^\beta}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
       \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^2)^{-\beta}\,dt\right\}^{1/2},
 \tag{1}
\]
and
\[
 |g(a)-g(b)|
 \le \frac{\|g\|_{H^\beta}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}|e^{-ita}-e^{-itb}|^2
                 (1+t^2)^{-\beta}\,dt\right\}^{1/2}.
 \tag{2}
\]
The integral in (1) is finite because \(\beta>3/2>1/2\), as required by \(\textnormal{def:exact-projected-class}\).  In (2), the integrand converges pointwise to zero as \(|a-b|\to0\) and is bounded by the integrable function \(4(1+t^2)^{-\beta}\).  Splitting the integral into a compact frequency interval, on which convergence is uniform, and its uniformly small tail proves that its right-hand side tends to zero uniformly over every fixed-radius Sobolev ball.  Thus each such ball is uniformly bounded and equicontinuous on \(\mathcal A\).

This also gives total boundedness without invoking any additional property of the model.  Indeed, for a prescribed \(\epsilon>0\), choose a finite spatial mesh of \(\mathcal A\) fine enough that the common modulus in (2) is at most \(\epsilon/3\), and quantize the uniformly bounded values at the mesh points in increments at most \(\epsilon/3\).  There are finitely many quantized arrays.  Two functions producing the same array differ by at most \(\epsilon\) everywhere on \(\mathcal A\), by applying (2) from an arbitrary point to a nearest mesh point.  Choosing one representative from each nonempty array therefore gives a finite uniform \(\epsilon\)-net.

We next verify that the relevant Sobolev balls are closed for uniform convergence.  Suppose \(g_m\) is supported in \(\mathcal A\), \(\|g_m\|_{H^\beta}\le R\), and \(g_m\to g\) uniformly on \(\mathcal A\).  The continuous representatives of the \(g_m\)'s vanish at the boundary of \(\mathcal A\), so the zero extension of \(g\) is continuous and
\[
 \|g_m-g\|_{L^2(\mathbb R)}
 \le (2B_A)^{1/2}\|g_m-g\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}
 \longrightarrow0.                                      \tag{3}
\]
Put \(h_m(t)=(1+t^2)^{\beta/2}\widehat g_m(t)\).  This is a bounded sequence in \(L^2(\mathbb R)\).  Expanding in a countable orthonormal basis, selecting a diagonal subsequence on which every coefficient converges, and using the common norm bound first for finite linear combinations and then by approximation, yields a weakly convergent subsequence \(h_{m_k}\rightharpoonup h\) with
\[
 \|h\|_2\le \liminf_{k\to\infty}\|h_{m_k}\|_2.          \tag{4}
\]
By (3) and the Fourier isometry, \(\widehat g_{m_k}\to\widehat g\) strongly in \(L^2\).  On the other hand, multiplication by \((1+t^2)^{-\beta/2}\) is a bounded operator on \(L^2\), so weak convergence of \(h_{m_k}\) gives
\[
 \widehat g_{m_k}\rightharpoonup(1+t^2)^{-\beta/2}h.
\]
Uniqueness of a weak limit and the strong convergence identify \(\widehat g=(1+t^2)^{-\beta/2}h\).  Hence \(g\in H^\beta(\mathbb R)\), and (4) gives \(\|g\|_{H^\beta}\le R\).  Therefore the fixed-support Sobolev ball is closed in the uniform metric.  Its total boundedness proved above, together with completeness of the uniform metric on continuous functions, proves its compactness.

Apply this conclusion with \(R=R_f\) and \(R=R_q\).  Uniform convergence on the common compact support preserves nonnegativity, the unit-integral condition because
\[
 \left|\int_{\mathcal A}(f_m-f)\right|
 \le 2B_A\|f_m-f\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)},                 \tag{5}
\]
the inequality \(f_x\ge\kappa\) on \(I\), and the joint domination constraint \(|q_x|\le B_Yf_x\).  Thus the joint signal-coordinate subset appearing in \(\mathscr K\) is closed in a finite product of compact spaces and is compact.  The mass vectors form a closed subset of the finite-dimensional simplex, since \(p_x\ge p_{\min}\) and \(\sum_xp_x=1\); hence they too form a compact set.

It remains to prove compactness of each error-law coordinate.  Let \((Q_m)\) be any sequence satisfying the \(q_e\)-moment bound in \(\textnormal{def:exact-projected-class}\).  Markov's inequality follows directly by integrating \(\mathbf 1\{|u|>R\}\le |u|^{q_e}R^{-q_e}\), and gives
\[
 \sup_m Q_m(|u|>R)\le M_eR^{-q_e}.                           \tag{6}
\]
We briefly give a direct subsequence construction.  For the distribution functions \(F_m\), diagonal selection over the rational numbers gives a subsequence, still indexed by \(m\), such that \(F_m(r)\) converges for every rational \(r\).  The monotone rational limits, made right-continuous by taking their infimum over rationals strictly to the right, define a distribution function \(F\); (6) forces its limits at negative and positive infinity to be zero and one.  The interval masses \(F(b)-F(a)\) therefore define a Borel probability law \(Q\).  At every continuity point \(u\) of \(F\), rational points on either side of \(u\) sandwich \(F_m(u)\) and show that \(F_m(u)\to F(u)\).  To verify weak convergence directly, choose \(R\) so that (6) makes the two tails uniformly small, partition \([-R,R]\) at continuity points of \(F\), and bound a bounded continuous test function above and below by its extrema on the partition intervals.  Uniform continuity on \([-R,R]\), followed by refinement of the partition and then \(R\to\infty\), shows
\[
 \int h\,dQ_m\longrightarrow\int h\,dQ
 \quad\text{for every bounded continuous }h.                \tag{7}
\]
Thus \(Q_m\) converges weakly to \(Q\).

For every \(L<\infty\), the function \(|u|^{q_e}\wedge L\) is bounded and continuous.  Equation (7), followed by monotone convergence in \(L\), yields
\[
 \int |u|^{q_e}\,dQ(u)
 =\sup_L\int(|u|^{q_e}\wedge L)\,dQ(u)
 \le M_e.                                                     \tag{8}
\]
Moreover, for every law under consideration, including the limit law by (8),
\[
 \int_{|u|>R}|u|\,dQ(u)
 \le R^{1-q_e}\int |u|^{q_e}\,dQ(u)
 \le M_eR^{1-q_e}.                                           \tag{9}
\]
Apply (7) to the bounded continuous clipping of the identity at levels \(-R\) and \(R\), and use (9) before sending \(R\to\infty\).  This proves convergence of first moments.  Consequently the condition \(\int u\,dQ_2(u)=0\) is closed.

The moment bound also gives, by the elementary inequality \(|e^{isu}-e^{itu}|\le|s-t||u|\) and the power-mean inequality,
\[
 |\phi_{Q_m}(s)-\phi_{Q_m}(t)|
 \le |s-t|\int|u|\,dQ_m(u)
 \le |s-t|M_e^{1/q_e}.                                       \tag{10}
\]
Weak convergence gives pointwise convergence of the characteristic functions by (7).  The common modulus (10), applied on a finite frequency mesh, upgrades this to uniform convergence on every compact frequency interval.  In particular,
\[
 \inf_{|t|\le\nu_0}|\phi_Q(t)|
 \ge c_0                                                        \tag{11}
\]
whenever the same inequality holds for every \(Q_m\).  Equations (6)--(11) prove sequential compactness, and closedness of all the imposed restrictions, for each error-law coordinate in the weak topology.  Since the topology is metrized by the metric specified in the claim, sequential compactness is compactness.  Combining the signal, mass, and two error-law coordinates proves compactness of \(\mathscr K\).

Now let \(\vartheta_m\to\vartheta\) in the asserted product metric.  Uniform signal convergence and common support give
\[
 \sup_{r\in\mathbb R}|\widehat f_{x,m}(r)-\widehat f_x(r)|
 \le 2B_A\|f_{x,m}-f_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}\to0,       \tag{12}
\]
and the same bound with \(q_x\) in place of \(f_x\).  Local uniform convergence of the error characteristic functions was proved after (10).  Since characteristic functions have modulus at most one, \(\int f_x=1\), and \(\int|q_x|\le B_Y\int f_x=B_Y\), (12) and the product identity imply local uniform convergence on \(\mathbb R^2\) of both fitted channels
\[
 (s,t)\longmapsto \widehat f_x(s+t)\phi_{Q_1}(s)\phi_{Q_2}(t),
 \qquad
 (s,t)\longmapsto \widehat q_x(s+t)\phi_{Q_1}(s)\phi_{Q_2}(t). \tag{13}
\]

For continuity of the profiled target, the lower bound \(f_x,f'_x\ge\kappa\) on \(I\) and the domination \(|q'_x|\le B_Yf'_x\), both from \(\textnormal{def:exact-projected-class}\), give
\[
 \left\|\frac{q_x}{f_x}-\frac{q'_x}{f'_x}\right\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \le \kappa^{-1}\|q_x-q'_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}
     +B_Y\kappa^{-1}\|f_x-f'_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}.   \tag{14}
\]
Also \(\|q'_x/f'_x\|_{L^\infty(I)}\le B_Y\).  Therefore, using the definition \(\mu_\vartheta=\sum_xp_xq_x/f_x\),
\[
 \|\mu_\vartheta-\mu_{\vartheta'}\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \le \sum_xp_x\left\|\frac{q_x}{f_x}-\frac{q'_x}{f'_x}\right\|_{L^\infty(I)}
      +B_Y\sum_x|p_x-p'_x|,                                  \tag{15}
\]
which tends to zero in the product metric.  This proves continuity into \(C(I)\).

Finally fix \(n\) and a realized sample \(z\).  By \(\textnormal{def:exact-joint-feasible-set}\), membership in \(\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)\) is the conjunction of finitely many mass and channel inequalities.  For example, the channel violation functions may be written
\[
 v^F_{x,s,t}(z,\vartheta)
 =\left(
 \left|\widehat F_{x,n}(z;s,t)
       -\widehat f_x(s+t)\phi_{Q_1}(s)\phi_{Q_2}(t)\right|
       -\rho^F_{x,n}(z)
 \right)_+,                                                   \tag{16}
\]
with \(v^G_{x,s,t}\) defined analogously, and the mass violations are
\[
 v^p_x(z,\vartheta)
 =\left(
 |p_x-\widehat p_x(z)|
 -\left\{\frac{\log(6|\mathcal X|/\alpha)}{2n}\right\}^{1/2}
 \right)_+.                                                   \tag{17}
\]
The empirical sums, counts, empty-cell convention, and radii in \(\textnormal{def:mass-confidence-region}\), \(\textnormal{def:upper-tuning-grid}\), and \(\textnormal{def:ecf-radii}\) are Borel measurable functions of \(z\).  Hence (16)--(17) are measurable in \(z\).  Equations (13) and continuity of the mass coordinates show that they are continuous in \(\vartheta\).  Their common zero set is exactly \(\Theta^{\mathrm{ex}}_{n,\alpha}(z)\).  It is therefore closed in the compact space \(\mathscr K\), and hence compact.  This also proves the asserted measurability and continuity of all the finitely many constraint-violation functions.
body.justification: Compactness is the deterministic substitute for a quantitative inverse modulus in the exact projected nuisance class.
body.gap: The finite relaxed sieve does not have a proved shrinking diameter, whereas exact class constraints admit a qualitative subsequence argument.
body.consumer: It supplies compact feasible values, continuous target profiling, and convergent subsequences for the qualitative diameter lemma and abstract exact-class band.
